name: Singapore
tagline: Everything in English — and a subsidy that comes with a three-year contract
summary: Singapore runs entirely in English and reads the IB directly. The headline price is not the price: international students can take the MOE Tuition Grant, which brings tuition at NUS and NTU down to about SGD 21,400–22,200 a year, in exchange for a contract, guaranteed by two sureties, to work for a Singapore entity for three years after graduating. You choose it by ticking a box on the application form. NUS closes 17 February 2027 and NTU 19 March 2027; LASALLE's arts window closes as early as 1 November 2026.
whyConsider: Every degree is taught in English, and NUS and NTU are large research universities with international reputations.
The MOE Tuition Grant cuts international tuition from roughly SGD 33,400–40,600 a year to roughly SGD 21,400–22,200 at NUS and NTU — if you accept the service obligation.

The IB is read directly: NUS treats the IB Diploma as its own applicant group with its own window, and SMU does not ask IB Diploma holders for SAT, IELTS or TOEFL — though its Law and Computing & Law degrees want English A at grade 6 or 7 (HL or SL), with shortfalls considered case by case.
The three-year service obligation is, viewed differently, a guaranteed graduate-employment pathway into Singapore's job market — and Singapore actively wants the people it has subsidised to stay.
SUTD, built with MIT, runs a genuinely unusual design-led engineering curriculum with no departments in the first year.
watchOuts: The Tuition Grant service obligation is a contract and it should be read as one. NTU states that a non-Singaporean who takes the grant signs an agreement that contractually obliges them to work in a Singapore entity for three years after graduating. MOE adds that only full-time employment after graduation counts, that a job search in Singapore typically takes about six months, and that deferring the bond for postgraduate study needs approval at least eight weeks in advance. Taking the grant is a decision about where you live into the 2030s.

You do not sign it alone. The agreement requires two sureties of any nationality, over 21 and under 65, not undischarged bankrupts, with the financial means to cover the liability — MOE encourages immediate family. You and your sureties are jointly liable for liquidated damages if the bond is not served.

The exposure is not only at the end. MOE states that a student who withdraws from the course midway is liable, with their sureties, for liquidated damages on the Tuition Grant received plus 10% compounded interest a year, with late-payment interest on top. Illness, homesickness or a change of mind in second year all fall inside that.

You elect the grant on the application form, months before anyone explains it, and sign the agreement in September or October once you are already in Singapore. By then you have flown, paid and moved in. Treat the tick-box as the decision point.

The deadlines are not shared and are not close together. LASALLE asks you to apply by 1 November 2026, NUS closes 17 February 2027, NTU closes 19 March 2027, and SUTD, SIT, SMU, SUSS and NAFA have not yet published 2027 dates (SMU's and SIT's 2026 cycles closed on 19 March 2026). There is no single date to remember and no portal that will remember it for you.

NTU will not consider a May-session IB candidate for Medicine, the Renaissance Engineering Programme, or Arts and Science (Academic Discipline & Education), because those decide before your results exist. That is a whole category of ambition closed off by a calendar.

Actual IB results are due at NTU within three days of release — the first week of July, in the middle of the Danish summer holiday. Both NTU and NUS make it mandatory to authorise the IB to release your transcript to them (NUS institute code 000690); ask your IB coordinator before July.
SUSS opens applications for its July 2027 intake in November 2026. James Cook University Singapore's 2027 dates are not given here: check its admissions page.
Tuition is given here for NTU (2026 entrants) and NUS (AY2026/2027 entrants) only. Do not assume NUS's or NTU's numbers apply to SMU or SUTD.

Whether an international student at LASALLE or NAFA can take the Tuition Grant, and would therefore be bonded, is not established. The University of the Arts Singapore names only Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents and refers the question back to the two colleges. Ask before you assume either way.
Yale-NUS College has closed — it took its final cohort in 2021 and no longer admits students. NUS College is the successor honours college, and it is a different thing.
Indicative grade profiles are published for the Singapore-Cambridge A-level, not usually for the IB. Ask admissions directly for the IB equivalent rather than trusting a figure from a forum.
Singapore is expensive to live in, off campus in particular. Campus accommodation is the realistic option and is not guaranteed for all years.

If you can claim Danish SU, it works differently for a full degree outside the EU/EEA. Check su.dk early. If you cannot claim it, check whether your own country's student finance covers a degree outside Europe.

ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Programme-specific HL requirements apply — engineering and computing normally want HL Mathematics, medicine wants HL Chemistry and Biology. Check each programme's own requirements.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: No published conversion table. IB points are read directly against a programme's indicative profile.
notes: The IB Diploma is a standard entry qualification for the international admissions route at the autonomous universities, and NUS goes further by treating it as its own applicant group with its own application window rather than lumping it in with other international qualifications.

Predicted grades are used for the initial assessment and offers are conditional on the final diploma. NTU requires the actual results within three days of their release in July, and both NTU and NUS require you to authorise the IB to send them your official transcript (NUS institute code 000690).
Some programmes are closed to a May-session IB candidate because they decide before results exist. NTU names Medicine, Renaissance Engineering, and Arts and Science (Academic Discipline & Education).
Official indicative IB grade profiles are not published; ask admissions for the published profile.
NUS requires English to be one of your IB subjects; SMU does not ask IB Diploma holders for IELTS, TOEFL or SAT; NTU's IB page sets no separate English test. Check the others with each university.

portal.name: No shared application — six autonomous universities, six forms, six fees, six deadlines. There is a shared acceptance: every offer you hold across them is settled once, in the Joint Acceptance Portal.

deadlines.label: LASALLE College of the Arts — main application window for the August 2027 intake
deadlines.notes: The earliest deadline on this page by a wide margin, and easy to miss. LASALLE opens on 1 October 2026 and asks you to apply by 1 November 2026, with outcomes announced by 23 December 2026 — eight months before IB results. LASALLE adds two hedges of its own: "the timeline provided serves as a general guide. Actual outcome release dates may vary", and that future application windows may open if programme seats remain available. So this is a window rather than the only chance, but it is the one that gets first pick of the seats, and the outcome dates are softer than the application ones. Music runs on its own later date and has its own entry below.

deadlines.label: Nanyang Technological University — application window for the August 2027 intake
deadlines.notes: NTU's own table for IB Diploma holders: online application 15 October 2026 to 19 March 2027, with programme choices, the application fee, the criminal records declaration and any scholarship application all due by 19 March 2027, supporting documents by 22 March 2027, and Art, Design and Media portfolio materials by 19 March 2027. Offers are released between March and May 2027. It opens two months before NUS. Application fee SGD 25 for international applicants.

deadlines.label: Nanyang Technological University — supporting documents due
deadlines.notes: Three days after the application itself. NTU states that an incomplete application after the deadline will not be considered. A fourth NTU date sits a further four days out and has its own entry below: the photograph and appraisal form on 26 March 2027.

deadlines.label: Nanyang Technological University — actual IB results due
deadlines.notes: NTU does not publish a calendar date. It says actual IB results must be submitted within three days of the results release in July 2027, and the IB releases on 6 July 2027, so 9 July 2027 is arithmetic on those two facts rather than a date NTU has printed. It is a very tight deadline and it lands in the Danish summer holiday. NTU also makes it mandatory to grant it direct access to your official transcripts through the IBO before July 2027, which is a separate action you take months earlier.

deadlines.label: National University of Singapore — IB Diploma application window, AY2027/2028
deadlines.notes: NUS runs the IB Diploma as its own applicant group with its own window, separate from the one for other international qualifications — although for AY2027/2028 both happen to run 16 December 2026 to 17 February 2027. It closes a month before NTU's. NUS says most applicants hear by the third week of May, and that IB applicants taking the May 2027 examination will hear by the third week of July 2027. On 23 September 2026 every AY2027/2028 window on NUS's page, including this one, was marked "[Closed]", three months before it is due to open; the status is probably left over from the previous cycle. NUS says to "check the information regularly below for the latest updates, as the details are subject to change." If you still see "[Closed]" in December 2026, write to the NUS Office of Admissions rather than assume you have missed it. One thing this page does settle for an IB candidate: the three-day final-results rule it imposes applies to Advanced Placement, Gaokao, HKDSE, Indian Standard 12 and STPM candidates and the IB is not on that list, so NUS, unlike NTU, sets no three-day turnaround on you.

deadlines.label: Singapore Management University — August 2027 intake
deadlines.notes: Not published yet. On 24 September 2026 SMU's IB Diploma page still showed only the AY2026-27 cycle: applications 17 November 2025 to 19 March 2026, teacher-provided predicted scores by 31 March 2026, interviews and decisions March to May, and acceptance by 25 May 2026 for first-window offers. Those are last cycle's dates; 2027's may differ. IB Diploma holders do not need SAT, IELTS or TOEFL.

deadlines.label: Singapore University of Technology and Design — 2027 admissions application window
deadlines.notes: SUTD's admissions page currently shows the 2026 window only: Singapore-Cambridge GCE A-Level from the day of release of A-Level results to 19 March 2026, and all other qualifications — which is where an IB Diploma sits — 2 January to 2 March 2026. That international window is two months long against NTU's five, and it closes seventeen days before SUTD's own domestic one. The 2027 equivalent is not published yet.

deadlines.label: Singapore Institute of Technology — August 2027 intake
deadlines.notes: SIT publishes its cycle one year at a time and currently shows 2026: online applications 8 January to 19 March 2026, interviews from mid-February to mid-May, outcomes mid-April to mid-May, acceptance 25 May 2026 and an appeal window 26 May to 2 June 2026. Every SIT applicant is interviewed. The 2027 dates are not published.

deadlines.label: Singapore University of Social Sciences — July 2027 intake
deadlines.notes: SUSS says applications for the July 2027 intake open in November 2026. The closing date is not out yet.

deadlines.label: LASALLE College of the Arts — BA (Hons) Music and Diploma in Music
deadlines.notes: Music runs four months behind the rest of LASALLE: both the BA (Hons) and the Diploma close on 28 February 2027, against 1 November 2026 for everything else. Outcomes are announced by 20 April 2027 for the BA (Hons) and 2 April 2027 for the Diploma, and shortlisted BA (Hons) applicants are invited to interview from February 2027 — so the interview invitations go out before the application even closes. LASALLE's MA Art Therapy closes on 31 January 2027, which is published on the same page and is mentioned here only so that it is not mistaken for an undergraduate date: it is a master's programme and is not open to a school leaver.

deadlines.label: Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts — August 2027 intake
deadlines.notes: NAFA's admissions guide on the site is the AY2026/27 one and nothing for 2027 is published yet. The University of the Arts Singapore, which now validates, confers and awards both NAFA's and LASALLE's degree programmes, says applications for the August 2026 intake are open and will close once all programme seats are filled, and that there is one intake commencing in August each year — so the shape of the 2027 cycle is a single August intake that closes when the seats go, not on a date.

deadlines.label: MOE Tuition Grant — elected on the admission application form
deadlines.notes: There is no separate date because there is no separate application: NTU states that international students who want the Tuition Grant must indicate they are opting for it in their online admission application form. Elect it at the moment you apply, or pay the unsubsidised fee. This is the point at which the three-year service obligation is chosen, months before anything is signed and long before anyone explains it to you.

deadlines.label: MOE Tuition Grant — accept the offer with or without the grant
deadlines.notes: A second decision point, after the offer. NTU set 17 July 2026 as the date by which a 2026 entrant had to say whether they accepted their place with or without the Tuition Grant. The 2027 equivalent is not published yet — but note where in the year it falls: eleven days after IB results, in the middle of the Danish summer.

deadlines.label: MOE Tuition Grant — sign the Tuition Grant Agreement with two sureties
deadlines.notes: The third and last point, and it happens after term has started. NTU's 2026 window for online signing on the TG&S Portal runs 19 September to 18 October 2026, with registration opening in September of the admitted year and requiring a Singpass, which itself needs a Student's Pass first. Two sureties must sign as well. MOE states that a student who does not complete the registration and signing will be charged the full unsubsidised fees. The 2027 window is not published.

deadlines.label: Joint Acceptance Exercise — accepting an autonomous university offer
deadlines.notes: The one genuinely shared step in Singapore admissions, and an easy one to overlook. You apply to each autonomous university separately, and then accept through a single Joint Acceptance Portal that lists every offer you hold across them. NUS shows two acceptance windows for AY2027/2028, both marked "To be Confirmed". SIT's 2026 equivalent was 25 May 2026, for context.

deadlines.label: James Cook University Singapore — 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: Not confirmed here; check JCU Singapore's application pages. It runs a trimester structure with several intakes a year rather than a single August one, so a missed date is less costly here than at an autonomous university.

deadlines.label: Curtin Singapore — 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: Not established. Curtin Singapore's admission page publishes its Private Education Institution registration — number 200804822R, valid 20 May 2026 to 19 May 2032 — and no application deadline. Curtin Singapore teaches on a trimester structure.

deadlines.label: DigiPen Institute of Technology Singapore — 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: Not established. DigiPen Singapore's admissions page showed no application deadline on 23 September 2026. Its degrees are awarded by DigiPen in the United States, so the academic calendar that governs is Redmond's rather than Singapore's.

deadlines.label: Singapore Institute of Management (SIM Global Education) — 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: SIM delivers partner universities' degrees and each partner runs its own intakes, so there is no one SIM date. Check the dates for the specific partner degree.

deadlines.label: ESSEC Business School Asia-Pacific — 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: Not listed here. The ESSEC Global BBA is admitted to through ESSEC in France, not through the Singapore campus, so its deadlines belong to the French admissions cycle; read them on the France page.

deadlines.label: IB results released
deadlines.notes: NTU takes your application on predicted grades and then requires the actual results within three days of release, in the middle of the Danish summer holiday. NUS is gentler and tells IB applicants sitting the May 2027 session that they will hear by the third week of July, and its own three-day rule names Advanced Placement, Gaokao, HKDSE, Indian Standard 12 and STPM and does not name the IB. LASALLE, by contrast, closed the previous November and never sees your results before it decides. The date is the IB's usual results day and is not yet confirmed by the IB for 2027.

deadlines.label: Nanyang Technological University — photograph and appraisal form due
deadlines.notes: A week after the application closes and four days after the supporting documents, and the last of NTU's four staggered deadlines. It is easy to miss because by 26 March 2027 a student believes the application is finished. The appraisal form is completed by somebody at your school, not by you, so it has to be requested in February.

steps: Work out which of the three Singapores you are applying to. The six Autonomous Universities, the two arts institutions under the University of the Arts Singapore, and the private institutions and foreign branch campuses run on different calendars, different rules and different money.
If the arts are in play, act first. LASALLE opens on 1 October 2026, two weeks before NTU, and asks you to apply by 1 November 2026, six weeks before NUS opens.

Decide about the MOE Tuition Grant with your family before you fill in any application form, because you elect it on the form itself. Taking it cuts tuition by roughly a third to almost half and commits you to three years of full-time work for a Singapore entity after graduation, guaranteed by two sureties who are jointly liable if you do not serve it.

Apply to each autonomous university separately, with predicted grades, transcript, personal statement and references, and a separate fee each time. NUS closes 17 February 2027; NTU closes 19 March 2027.
Check the programme is open to a May-session IB candidate. NTU excludes Medicine, Renaissance Engineering, and Arts and Science (Academic Discipline & Education) outright.
Authorise the IB organisation to send your transcript directly to the university. NTU requires this before July 2027 and will not release an outcome without it.
Expect an interview, portfolio or written test for the selective routes — SUTD and SIT interview as a matter of course, and NUS Law, medicine and the scholars’ programmes all add assessment.
Keep the first fortnight of July 2027 clear. NTU wants your actual results within three days of release.
Accept one offer through the Joint Acceptance Portal. The windows for 2027 are not yet announced.

Apply for a Student’s Pass through ICA’s SOLAR system once the university sponsors you, then register and sign the Tuition Grant Agreement in Singapore in the autumn — it needs a Singpass, which needs the Student’s Pass first.
Apply for campus accommodation the day your offer arrives. It is allocated separately and is the only realistic first-year option.
application.selectionNotes: Academic, with assessment layered on. NUS and NTU are large and selective and decide largely on grades; SMU is specialised in business, law, economics, social science and computing; SUTD assesses holistically on academics, traits and a portfolio with an interview for selected candidates, and says its approach is significantly different from most universities; SIT interviews every shortlisted applicant. LASALLE and NAFA decide on portfolio and audition, and their deadlines fall months before everyone else’s.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: All of them. English is the medium of instruction across the entire Singapore higher education system.
language.englishProof: NUS requires English to be one of your IB subjects; SMU does not ask IB Diploma holders for IELTS, TOEFL or SAT; NTU's IB page sets no separate English test. Check the others with each university.
notes: Singapore has four official languages but the universities operate entirely in English.
You will hear Singlish everywhere and pick it up whether you want to or not. It is not a barrier.

tuitionEuEea.value: Singapore does not differentiate by EU status — the categories are Singapore Citizen, Singapore Permanent Resident and International Student. As a European applicant you are an International Student.

tuitionNonEu.value: NTU, for students accepted in 2026, with the tuition fee fixed at the 2026 rate for the whole degree: International Student with the MOE Tuition Grant roughly SGD 21,400–21,800 per year; International Student without the grant SGD 36,350 (non-lab) to SGD 40,600 (lab-based) per year, inclusive of 9% GST. Medicine, non-subsidised only, SGD 91,250 per year for non-ASEAN internationals. Renaissance Engineering, non-subsidised only, SGD 32,000. NUS, for students admitted in AY2026/2027 (fixed for the cohort): international students with the Tuition Grant SGD 21,400 a year in computing, engineering and humanities and sciences, SGD 22,200 in business, SGD 30,450 in law; without the grant SGD 33,400–39,700 (SGD 44,450 law), inclusive of GST. AY2027/2028 fees are published in February to April 2027. SMU and SUTD figures are not given here.
tuitionNonEu.year: AY2026/27 entrants, fixed for the degree duration (NTU and NUS)

costs.applicationFee: Per university: NTU SGD 25 for international applicants. Check the others with each university.
notes: The NTU table distinguishes lab-based from non-lab programmes and ASEAN from other international students. Read it directly rather than relying on a single headline figure — and note that the published table's lab/non-lab labelling is worth double-checking against the PDF.
The key number is the difference between the two columns: roughly SGD 15,000–19,000 a year, or SGD 60,000–75,000 over a four-year degree. That is what the three-year service obligation is worth.
Non-subsidised fees include 9% GST; subsidised fees are quoted exclusive of it.
NTU states that the annual tuition fee is fixed at the year-of-entry rate for the duration of the degree, which removes the risk of mid-degree increases.
No official living-cost figure is quoted here. Campus accommodation is considerably cheaper than the private rental market, which is expensive.

funding: MOE Tuition Grant — the main subsidy and the main commitment. International students elect it on the admission application form, confirm it when accepting the offer, and then sign a Tuition Grant Agreement with two sureties that contractually obliges them to work in a Singapore entity for three years after graduation. At NTU it takes the fee from roughly SGD 36,350–40,600 a year to roughly SGD 21,400–21,800 — about SGD 60,000–75,000 across a four-year degree. It runs for the normal programme duration only, so a repeated year is unsubsidised.

Declining the grant is a real option, not a failure. You pay the full unsubsidised fee, you carry no obligation and you need no sureties. That is the right choice if you intend to return to Europe after graduating, and it should be a decision rather than a default.

Breaking the bond, or withdrawing from the course, makes you and both sureties liable for liquidated damages — on the outstanding bond period if you break it, and on the whole grant received plus 10% compounded interest a year if you withdraw mid-course.

Merit scholarships: NUS, NTU and SMU all run competitive scholarships for outstanding international entrants, typically covering tuition plus a living allowance. Most carry their own bond conditions — sometimes six years rather than three. Check each one’s terms before applying.

ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarships and similar regional awards are for nationals of ASEAN countries, so they are not open to EU/EEA citizens; if you hold another nationality, check the eligibility list.
Whether the Tuition Grant reaches LASALLE, NAFA or the private institutions for an international student is not established here.

funding.note: A full degree outside the EU/EEA follows separate rules, with its own ties-to-Denmark form: check su.dk before budgeting.

funding: Part-time work is restricted on a Student’s Pass — see workRights. Do not plan to fund yourself by working.
workRights: Full-time students on a Student's Pass at the institutions MOM lists (NUS and NTU among them) may work up to 16 hours a week in term without a work pass, and without a limit during vacations. Once the Student's Pass expires, a work pass is needed. Work is not a realistic way to close a funding gap in Singapore.
residency: EU citizenship gives no advantage. Once you accept an offer, the university sponsors your Student's Pass application through ICA's SOLAR system, which must be completed before you travel. On arrival you complete formalities at ICA and receive the pass. Many European citizens, Danes included, do not need a visa to enter Singapore as a visitor (check ICA's list for your nationality), but you cannot study on a visitor pass.
housing: Campus accommodation — halls of residence at NUS and NTU, the residential colleges, and SUTD's housing — is the only sensible first-year option and is allocated separately from the admission. It is not guaranteed for all four years at every university, and some allocate by a points system based on participation in campus activities. The private market in Singapore is expensive and usually means a room in a shared HDB flat. Apply for housing the day your offer arrives.
healthcare: International students are normally required to be covered by the university's own medical insurance scheme, charged as a compulsory fee alongside tuition. Singapore's healthcare is not free at the point of use, and your EHIC does not apply. Check what the university scheme actually covers — it is usually hospitalisation rather than routine care.

institutions.name: National University of Singapore
institutions.englishBachelors: All programmes, across a comprehensive range of faculties.
institutions.note: A comprehensive university on a large hillside campus in the west, whose honours college, NUS College, succeeded the closed Yale-NUS. It treats the IB Diploma as its own applicant group (window 16 December 2026 to 17 February 2027 for AY2027/2028, outcomes for May-session candidates by the third week of July 2027), and AY2026/27 international entrants paid SGD 21,400 a year with the Tuition Grant in most faculties.

institutions.name: Nanyang Technological University
institutions.englishBachelors: All programmes: engineering, science, business (Nanyang Business School), humanities, medicine (Lee Kong Chian) and education.
institutions.note: Apply on predicted grades by 19 March 2027; actual results are due within three days of release. Internationals pay roughly SGD 21,400–21,800 a year with the MOE Tuition Grant or SGD 36,350–40,600 without, fixed at the year-of-entry rate for the whole degree, and a May-session IB candidate may not apply to Medicine, Renaissance Engineering, or Arts and Science (Academic Discipline & Education) at all.

institutions.name: Singapore Management University
institutions.englishBachelors: Business Management, Accountancy, Economics, Law, Information Systems, Computing and Social Sciences.
institutions.note: Seminar teaching, a city-centre campus and compulsory internships, with a strong finance and consulting pipeline. It has an IB Diploma page of its own, does not ask IB holders for SAT or English tests, and interviews shortlisted applicants; its 2027 dates are not yet published.

institutions.name: Singapore University of Technology and Design
institutions.englishBachelors: Architecture and Sustainable Design, Engineering Product Development, Engineering Systems and Design, Computer Science and Design, and Design and Artificial Intelligence.
institutions.note: Founded with MIT, with a common design-centred first year before you choose a pillar. Admission is a holistic review of academics, traits and a portfolio, with personal insight questions and an interview for selected candidates, which needs months of preparation; its 2026 international window ran only 2 January to 2 March, and the 2027 one is not yet published.

institutions.name: Singapore Institute of Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: Applied degrees in engineering, health and social sciences, infocomm technology, food technology and hospitality — many with an integrated work-study year.
institutions.note: Singapore’s applied-sciences university, built around long industry placements, with a new campus in Punggol. It interviews every shortlisted applicant, its intake is overwhelmingly domestic polytechnic graduates, and its whole 2026 cycle — application, interview, offer, acceptance on 25 May — finished before IB results were released.

institutions.name: Singapore University of Social Sciences
institutions.englishBachelors: Social sciences, business, law, human development and early childhood education, with both full-time and part-time routes.
institutions.note: The sixth autonomous university, focused on social impact and lifelong learning. Its part-time and flexible structure is unusual, but its full-time intake is small and mostly domestic.

institutions.name: LASALLE College of the Arts
institutions.englishBachelors: BA (Hons) degrees across fine art, design, film, animation, fashion, music, dance and theatre. Degrees are now validated, conferred and awarded by the University of the Arts Singapore, the alliance of LASALLE and NAFA, rather than by Goldsmiths, University of London as they were until the 2024 intake.
institutions.note: An art school near Bugis with portfolio and audition entry. The August 2027 window opens 1 October 2026 and asks you to apply by 1 November 2026, the earliest date on this page, with outcomes by 23 December; Music closes later, on 28 February 2027.

institutions.name: Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts
institutions.englishBachelors: Degrees in art, design, music, dance and theatre, validated, conferred and awarded by the University of the Arts Singapore, the alliance of NAFA and LASALLE.
institutions.note: The older of Singapore’s two art academies, strong in music and Chinese-influenced visual art. It is now federated with LASALLE into the University of the Arts Singapore, and its 2027 dates are not published: the admissions guide on its site is still the AY2026/27 one.

institutions.name: James Cook University Singapore
institutions.englishBachelors: Australian JCU degrees in business, psychology, IT, environmental science and aquaculture, taught on the Singapore campus.
institutions.note: An Australian university's full branch campus, awarding the same degree as Townsville, on trimesters that let you finish a bachelor's in two years. No MOE Tuition Grant applies, because it is not an autonomous university.

institutions.name: Curtin Singapore
institutions.englishBachelors: Curtin University (Australia) degrees in business, commerce, marketing, mass communication and management.
institutions.note: Another Australian branch campus, business-focused and with a trimester structure that compresses the degree. A pragmatic route into an Australian qualification without moving to Australia.

institutions.name: DigiPen Institute of Technology Singapore
institutions.englishBachelors: BS in Computer Science in Real-Time Interactive Simulation, BA in Game Design, BFA in Digital Art and Animation, BS in Computer Science and Game Design.
institutions.note: The Singapore campus of the American games-technology institute, small and intensive. Degrees are awarded by DigiPen in the United States.

institutions.name: Singapore Institute of Management (SIM Global Education)
institutions.englishBachelors: External degrees awarded by partner universities including the University of London, RMIT, the University of Birmingham and the University at Buffalo.
institutions.note: Not a university in its own right — it delivers partner universities' degrees in Singapore. Useful if you want a British or Australian degree at Singapore prices, but you are not getting a Singapore university qualification and no MOE Tuition Grant applies.

institutions.name: ESSEC Business School Asia-Pacific
institutions.englishBachelors: The ESSEC Global BBA can be taken partly or largely on the Singapore campus, with the degree awarded by ESSEC in France.
institutions.note: A French grande école running a full Asian campus, which means a European degree with an Asian base and the option to move between Cergy, Rabat and Singapore. Worth considering if you want Asia without leaving the European qualification framework.
